sections.html:
Logan is the Cache County seat, about 47 miles north of Ogden and 82 miles north of Salt Lake City, on the Logan River at the foot of the Bear River Mountains. The 2020 count was 52,778 people and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 55,576. The median age was 24.2, and Utah State University shapes the rental market, so many sellers are landlords or heirs of a house near campus.

Streets on the east side climb across benches of old Lake Bonneville sediment, while the flat west side is closer to farmland and marsh. Lots on the benches raise slope and runoff questions at inspection, and lots in the west sit near wet ground, so walk your own lot after a storm and note where water collects before a buyer's inspector does.

Logan has warm, usually dry summers and cold winters with moderate snow: about 18.97 inches of precipitation and 61.5 inches of snow a year. The record low is minus 25 degrees. Roofs carry snow for months, and pipes in a vacant house can freeze. If you cannot heat or check on an empty house through the cold months, closing before winter may be the safer plan.

sections.h2: Utah State University and the rental market
sections.html:
Utah State University and its Space Dynamics Laboratory are the largest employers, and the main campus covers roughly 600 acres at the mouth of Logan Canyon. Other employers include ICON Health and Fitness, Campbell Scientific, Logan Regional Hospital, JBS USA, Schreiber Foods and Thermo Fisher Scientific. A seller with a rental near campus should think about the academic calendar when choosing a closing date.

Logan City School District runs eight public schools, and Cache County School District serves some Logan neighborhoods too, so confirm the boundary for your address. Connect Transit runs 15 zero-fare routes through Logan, North Logan and River Heights.

Every owner of a rental unit must hold a Logan landlord business license, and each ownership entity such as an LLC, trust or corporation needs its own. The exception covers an owner-occupied home rented only during a hospital or nursing home stay, or a temporary absence of three years or less.

Logan rental ruleLimit or requirement
Occupancy, most zonesThree unrelated people, or one family plus one additional person
Occupancy, Campus Residential zonesUp to six unrelated people, no more than two per bedroom
Notice of limitsIn the lease or on a zoning occupancy disclosure form
Request by code official or policeLease or form provided within seven days

Rentals must also meet the Fit Premise Ordinance in Municipal Code Chapter 15.25, and units that were not legally created may need to apply for grandfathered status. Changes to ownership or agent contact details need an amendment form from business licensing at 435-716-9230, Logan City Hall, 290 N 100 W. An investor buying your rental will ask for the license and occupancy paperwork, so make sure it is current.

The calendar is simple. Valuation notices go out in July, appeals run from August to September, tax notices arrive in October and payment is due November 30. Current-year taxes turn delinquent in December. Prior-year delinquent taxes are posted in January, and the Treasurer collects them or notifies new owners by the end of that month.

Utah takes 45 percent off the market value of a primary home, with a 183 consecutive day residency test. A buyer files Form TC-473A by September 15 after the sale, and counties cannot accept late filings.

The Cache County Recorder files the deed, and a state change added $5 to county recording fees, so ask for the current total. If you owe taxes when you sell, the title company pays them from your proceeds at closing, so there is nothing separate for you to chase down.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Logan
sections.html:
A Logan cash sale is an ordinary closing with no mortgage lender in the middle. The buyer reviews the property, makes an offer, and a title company handles liens, taxes and the deed.

  • Describe the house and any tenants or lease dates.
  • Review the offer and the closing date.
  • Close with a title company and have the deed recorded in Cache County.

Rental owners with a lease running to a set date, heirs managing from afar and owners who would rather not pay for repairs most often choose this route. A buyer who takes the house with tenants in place can ask for the lease and the occupancy disclosure form.

You skip the lender's appraisal, the bank's repair list, the staging and the open houses. With a student rental, you also skip the awkward task of showing rooms to strangers while tenants live there. The title work stays, and you decide the closing date, whether you want it soon or after the lease ends.

sections.h2: Selling a Logan house with tenants
sections.html:
A lease does not end because the owner decides to sell. Read it first and note the end date, the deposit and any renewal rights. A cash buyer can take the house with tenants in place, which spares you from asking students to leave early or from timing a closing around the school year. If you want the house empty, a cash buyer is also more flexible about waiting until the lease ends.

Hand the title company a copy of each lease so the deposit can be credited to the buyer at closing. Tell tenants in writing when the sale is happening and whom to contact afterward, so rent goes to the right place.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html: Pull together the deed or trust papers, the landlord license, the lease and the zoning occupancy disclosure form, your latest tax notice and any code notices. Add notes on the roof age and the heating system, since winter wear is the first thing a buyer asks about. A short folder of papers shortens the title work and answers an investor's first round of questions before they are asked.

An open tax bill is not a roadblock. Ask the Cache County Treasurer for the payoff and give it to the title officer. The amount is subtracted from your check, and the year is divided between you and the buyer so each of you carries only your own months.

Brigham Young sent settlers in 1859, and Logan was incorporated on January 17, 1866. The Cache County Historic Courthouse went up in 1883, the Logan Utah Temple was completed in 1884, and the Agricultural College of Utah, now Utah State University, opened on September 2, 1890. Cache County leads Utah in dairy products and is a major producer of hay, alfalfa and grain.

faqs.q: How many people live in Logan, Utah?
faqs.a: The estimate is 55,576 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 count was 52,778.

faqs.q: Do I need a landlord license to rent a house in Logan?
faqs.a: Yes. Logan requires a landlord business license for every owner of a rental unit, with a narrow exception for a temporary absence of three years or less. Call 435-716-9230 for fees and renewal.

faqs.q: When are Cache County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By November 30. The Treasurer mails tax notices in October, and unpaid current-year taxes become delinquent in December.

faqs.q: How many unrelated people can live in a Logan house?
faqs.a: Generally three unrelated people, or one family plus one more person. Campus Residential zones allow up to six, with no more than two per bedroom.

faqs.q: What is the largest employer in Logan?
faqs.a: Utah State University and its Space Dynamics Laboratory are the largest employers in Logan.
